notes: Template: ABox contraction on a many-valued relation (borders: symmetric, cardinality:many). Removes 'The Czech Republic borders Austria', a stored fact. Cardinality question: another neighbour the model holds (Germany); removing one value of a many-valued relation says nothing about the others, so the answer stays yes (new_answer equals original_answer). Related: whether Lower Austria borders the Czech Republic (composition through the bridge that Lower Austria is a state of Austria): a stored fact about a different individual whose border is part of the country's, so it is given up with it. Its stored status rests on the co-occurrence of 'Lower Austria' and 'Czech Republic' in both corpora. Derived: two binding questions that name the subject by a description the model holds separately (its capital, its first president); both answers are worked out, not stated. No composition is used: composition follows the edit to a single value and looks up a fact about it, but borders is many-valued, so 'the country the Czech Republic borders' picks out no single value; a description of the removed value ('the country whose capital is Vienna') would only ask the removed fact again with the object renamed, which README's binding (subject only) does not cover. Yes/no questions are the natural form for the own queries because the relation is many-valued: a wh-question ('Which country does the Czech Republic border?') has four answers. The edit is the Czech-Austrian border because it has no route back to 'yes' (the Slovak border, for example, could be rebuilt from the stored split of Czechoslovakia). The descriptions avoid geographic leaks: the Vltava (which runs along the Bohemian Forest near the Austrian border) and Brno (near the border) are not used. The propositional negation is worded 'Is it true that ... does not ...?'.
